caption: Algorithm S1. Full-Recompute Flow Field (C-FF)
rows:
Input: grid G, canonical goal set T, legal-move relation N(.)
Output: integration J, owner O, and next-cell direction D
1   Allocate fresh arrays; set J[v] <- INF, O[v] <- NIL, and D[v] <- NIL for every v in V
2   Q <- empty deterministic min-heap
3   for each walkable goal t in T, in canonical order do
4       J[t] <- 0; O[t] <- t; push the current record for t into Q
5   while Q is not empty do
6       u <- pop a record from Q; if stale, continue
7       for each legal predecessor p of u do
8           candidate <- c(p, u) + J[u]
9           if (candidate, O[u]) improves (J[p], O[p]) then
10              J[p] <- min(J[p], candidate); O[p] <- O[u]; push the revised p into Q
11  for each walkable, reachable, non-goal cell v do
12      S <- {s in N(v) : c(v, s) + J[s] equals J[v]}
13      D[v] <- deterministic minimum of S by (total, owner, remainder, coordinate)
14      assert O[v] equals O[D[v]]
15  return (J, O, D)
On every accepted grid change, build a fresh field by lines 1-15, then replace the old field.
A plan query follows D until the declared owner goal and requires J to decrease at each step.

caption: Algorithm S2. Incremental Dynamic Flow Field (IDFF)
rows: Algorithm S2. Incremental Dynamic Flow Field (IDFF)

Input: updated grid G; change set C; persistent field, Q, revisions, dirty set, cursor
Output: a queryable field or a resumable PENDING state
1   For a new change set, mark repair pending and make the field non-queryable
2   A <- changed cells and their clipped 3 x 3 dependency neighborhoods
3   for each v in A, mark its direction dirty; UPDATE-VERTEX(v)
4   while the queue phase is unfinished do
5       if the budget expired then preserve state and return PENDING
6       u <- pop the next non-stale inconsistent vertex, if any
7       if none remains then sort dirty cells, set cursor to 0, and end this phase
8       else if (rhs[u], rhsOwner[u]) precedes (g[u], gOwner[u]) then
9           (g[u], gOwner[u]) <- (rhs[u], rhsOwner[u]); invalidate u's queue revision
10      else (g[u], gOwner[u]) <- (INF, NIL); UPDATE-VERTEX(u)
11      if u was processed, UPDATE-VERTEX each predecessor
12      if u was processed, mark its changed direction dependencies dirty
13  while dirty cells remain from the saved cursor do
14      if the budget expired then preserve state and return PENDING
15      v <- next dirty cell; advance cursor; clear D[v]
16      if v is walkable, reachable, and not a goal then
17          D[v] <- deterministic successor s with c(v, s) + g[s] equal to g[v]
18  clear pending and dirty state; expose the field; return COMPLETE
UPDATE-VERTEX(v):
19  if v is a walkable goal then (rhs[v], rhsOwner[v]) <- (0, v)
20  else use the best legal successor via g; blocked/no successor gives (INF, NIL)
21  increment v's revision, invalidating its older queue entries
22  if g and rhs cost/owner pairs differ, enqueue v with the revised key
A resume skips lines 1-3 and retains its queue phase and direction cursor.
A plan call resumes pending repair before following the consistent direction field.

Algorithm S3. Managed multi-query execution with private lane state
rows: Algorithm S3. Managed multi-query execution with private lane state

Input: algorithm A in {C-FF, IDFF}, 16 frozen lane inputs B, worker count W, CPU plan P
Output: complete-batch time T and validated results R[0..15], or batch failure
1   Load and verify B and cached oracle outcomes before batch timing
2   Create W fixed workers; worker j binds to P[j], signals READY, and waits
3   Coordinator waits for every READY signal; start clock; release workers
4   In parallel, each worker j executes lanes i = j, j + W, ... < 16:
5       if batch failure is already flagged: skip each unstarted lane
6       otherwise verify the worker CPU binding and enter the lane
7       Deserialize private B[i]; build private grid G; create planner A
8       try:
9           Initialize A; require valid status, budget, and grid version
10          Run all initial queries; validate paths and record outcomes
11          for each of the 24 event groups in frozen order:
12              for each atomic partition in its prescribed order:
13                  Require no pending repair; apply the changes to G
14                  Call A.ApplyChanges using the technical budget
15                  Require completed repair, valid budget, matching versions
16              Run all fixed-start queries; validate paths; record outcomes
17          Require the full query and repair counts; store result R[i]
18       finally: reset the lane planner
19       On a lane error: flag batch failure; stop admitting unstarted lanes
20       Fingerprint successful results; verify the ending CPU binding
21       On a binding error: flag batch failure
22   Each worker clears its binding and signals DONE after its lane loop
23   Coordinator waits for all DONE signals; stop clock at T; join workers
24   Require 16 completed lanes, no failed/skipped lanes, and valid bindings
25   Compare every recorded query with its cached oracle after timing
26   If any check fails: reject the complete batch; do not retry or replace
27   Return T and results in ascending lane order
Within a lane, C-FF and IDFF execute the serial procedures of Algorithms S1 and S2.
